entries.name: mcp__umbraco__create-media
entries.description:
Upload any media file to Umbraco (images, documents, audio, video, SVG, or custom types).

  Pick the sourceType that matches where the file lives:
  - If the file is attached to this chat or you just generated it → sourceType="file" (the host fills in the file reference automatically).
  - If you have a public direct-download URL → sourceType="url".
  - For tiny inline payloads (≤10 KiB decoded) → sourceType="base64".

  Media Types:
  - Image: jpg, png, gif, webp, etc. (supports cropping)
  - Article: pdf, docx, doc (documents)
  - Audio: mp3, wav, etc.
  - Video: mp4, webm, etc.
  - SVG: svg files only
  - File: any other file type
  - Custom: any custom media type created in Umbraco

  Source Types:
  1. filePath - Most efficient for local files, works with any size
     SECURITY: Requires UMBRACO_ALLOWED_MEDIA_PATHS environment variable
     to be configured with comma-separated allowed directories.
     Example: UMBRACO_ALLOWED_MEDIA_PATHS="/tmp/uploads,/var/media"
  2. url - Stream from any public direct-download URL (Drive / Dropbox / etc.). Use this for anything above 10 KiB that isn't already attached to the chat.
  3. file - Stream a host-attached file. The connector injects { download_url, file_id, mime_type, file_name } on the 'file' field automatically when the user attached a file or you generated one in this chat — prefer this over url for chat-bound files.
  4. base64 - ONLY for tiny inline payloads; server hard-rejects decoded base64 over 10 KiB to prevent LLM-truncated corrupt files.

  The tool automatically:
  - Creates temporary files
  - Detects and validates media types (auto-corrects SVG vs Image)
  - Configures correct property editors (ImageCropper vs UploadField)
  - Cleans up temporary files

sourceType.description: Media source type: 'filePath' for local files (Node stdio only), 'url' for public direct-download URLs (streamed; preferred for everything not already attached to the chat), 'file' for host-injected attachments — the connector populates the 'file' object automatically when the user attached a file or you generated one in this chat, 'base64' for TINY inline payloads only — the server rejects base64 above 10 KiB decoded to stop LLM-truncated or thumbnail-preview base64 from persisting as corrupt files

name.description: The name of the media item

mediaTypeName.description: Media type: 'Image', 'Article', 'Audio', 'Video', 'SVG', 'File', or custom media type name

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file (required if sourceType is 'filePath')

fileUrl.description: [raw] Public, direct-download URL to fetch the file from (required if sourceType is 'url'). Must be reachable without authentication. Share/viewer links (e.g. drive.google.com/file/d/<id>/view, Dropbox ?dl=0, OneDrive view URLs) must be converted to their direct-download equivalent first — Google Drive: drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=<id>. Uploads are streamed, so multi-MB files round-trip without timing out.

file.description: [raw] Host-injected file object (required if sourceType is 'file'). ChatGPT's connector populates this automatically when the user attached a file or you generated one in this chat — leave it for the host to fill, do not synthesise it yourself.

download_url.description: Temporary URL the host provides to fetch the file bytes

file_id.description: Persistent file identifier from the host

mime_type.description: MIME type if the host knows it

file_name.description: Original file name if the host knows it

fileAsBase64.description: Base64-encoded file data (required if sourceType is 'base64'). HARD LIMIT: decoded payload must be ≤10 KiB; the server rejects anything larger because LLMs reliably truncate big base64 strings or substitute thumbnail previews, both producing corrupt files. Use sourceType='url' or 'file' for everything bigger.

entries.name: mcp__umbraco__update-and-publish-document
entries.description:
Updates a document by Id and publishes it in a single operation.

  IMPORTANT: If workflow approval is required, use update-document followed by initiate-workflow-action instead.
  This function bypasses approval workflows and publishes directly to the live site.

  ### Cultures To Publish
  - culturesToPublish controls which of the document's variants get published.
  - Umbraco only accepts real culture codes here - wildcards ("*") and nulls are rejected with an error.
  - When the document does not vary by culture (invariant content), pass an empty array `[]` to publish the single invariant variant.
  - When the document varies by culture, provide the culture codes of the variants you want published.

  If you must use this tool:
  - Always read the current document value first
  - Only update the required values
  - Don't miss any properties from the original document

entries.name: mcp__umbraco__update-document
entries.description:
Updates a document by Id. USE AS LAST RESORT ONLY.

  IMPORTANT: Prefer these specialized tools instead:
  - update-document-name: For renaming a document (or a specific culture variant) - the safe way to change the name
  - update-document-properties: For updating individual property values (simpler, safer)
  - update-block-property: For updating properties within BlockList/BlockGrid/RichText blocks

  Only use this tool when you need to update document-level metadata (template, variants)
  or when the specialized tools cannot handle your specific use case.

  If you must use this tool:
  - Always read the current document value first
  - Only update the required values
  - Don't miss any properties from the original document
  - WARNING: passing an empty "values" array will DELETE all existing property values on the document.
    Always include the full, unmodified "values" array from the document you just read unless you
    intend to clear every property. If the document currently has values, an empty "values" array is
    rejected unless "confirmClearValues" is set to true.

confirmClearValues.description: Must be set to true to proceed when 'data.values' is an empty array and the document currently has property values. Without this, the call is rejected to prevent accidentally wiping every property value - the exact mistake that motivated this guard. Not needed if the document has no existing values, or if 'data.values' is non-empty.

input.name: MCP Is the USB-C Port for AI

values.value: Before MCP, every AI integration was a custom cable. One open protocol turns an N-times-M integration mess into plug and play.
Claude
MCP Is the USB-C Port for AI
One open protocol, and every tool you own becomes something an AI can plug into.

value.markup:
The problem: every integration was a custom cable

A language model on its own can only talk. To do real work it has to reach things: your files, your database, your CMS, your issue tracker. For years that meant bespoke glue. Every AI application wrote its own connector for every system, and every system vendor was asked to support every AI application.

That is the classic N × M problem. Ten AI clients and ten systems means a hundred integrations, each with its own auth quirks, its own schema and its own bugs.

The fix: agree on the plug

The Model Context Protocol, introduced by Anthropic as an open standard in late 2024, replaces that grid with a single contract. A system exposes an MCP server once. Any MCP client can then use it. N × M becomes N + M.

values.value: Life before a standard plug. Photo from Unsplash.
Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications.
modelcontextprotocol.io

value.markup:
Three things a server can offer

  • Tools are actions the model can call, such as create-document or publish-document. Each one ships with a JSON Schema, so the model knows exactly what arguments are valid.
  • Resources are data the client can read, such as files, records or API responses.
  • Prompts are reusable templates a server can hand to the user.

Why it is awesome

  • Build once, use everywhere. The same server works in every MCP-capable client.
  • Self-describing. Tools are discovered at runtime. Add a tool to the server and the agent can use it right away.
  • Local or remote. Servers run as a local process over stdio or as a remote service over HTTP.
  • Open. The specification and SDKs are public, so nobody owns the plug.

Standards are rarely exciting. This one is, because of what it unlocks: an assistant that stops describing the work and starts doing it.

input.name: This Blog Was Built Without Opening the Backoffice

values.value: Five blocks, two page types, a block grid, five images and three published pages. All of it created by an agent through the Umbraco MCP server.
Claude
This Blog Was Built Without Opening the Backoffice
What it looks like when a CMS speaks MCP and an agent is handed the keys.

value.markup:
The brief

The instruction was one paragraph: spin up a simple blog, build everything with blocks and the block grid, and write two posts about why MCP is awesome. You are reading the second one.

What the agent actually did

  1. Modeled the content. Five element types (hero, rich text, image, quote, post list), a block grid data type that allows them, and two page types with templates.
  2. Filed everything where it belongs. Blocks went into the Blocks folder and pages into Pages, following the project's own rules.
  3. Pulled in media. Images were streamed from Unsplash straight into a media folder.
  4. Wrote and published. A front page and two posts, each assembled from blocks, plus a domain so the site answers on the root url.

Every one of those steps was an MCP tool call against the Umbraco Management API.

values.value: I did not click a single button. I read the schema, called the tools, and read the result back to check my work.
The agent that built this site
The editor stays in charge. Photo from Unsplash.

value.markup:
Why this matters for a CMS

  • The boring parts disappear. Scaffolding document types and seeding realistic content takes minutes.
  • It is real content. Nothing here is a mock-up. Editors can open any page in the backoffice and keep working on it, block by block.
  • The rules still apply. The agent works through the same API, permissions and validation as everyone else, and the project conventions are written down where it can read them.
  • It is verifiable. Every write can be read back. When a payload is wrong, the agent sees that and corrects it.

The takeaway

MCP does not replace the editor or the developer. It removes the distance between deciding what should exist and having it exist. That is why it is awesome.

The brief

The instruction was one paragraph: spin up a simple blog, build everything with blocks and the block grid, and write two posts about why MCP is awesome. You are reading the second one.

What the agent actually did

  1. Modeled the content. Five element types (hero, rich text, image, quote, post list), a block grid data type that allows them, and two page types with templates.
  2. Filed everything where it belongs. Blocks went into the Blocks folder and pages into Pages, following the project's own rules.
  3. Pulled in media. Images were streamed from Unsplash straight into a media folder.
  4. Wrote and published. A front page and two posts, each assembled from blocks, plus a domain so the site answers on the root url.

Every one of those steps was an MCP tool call against the Umbraco Management API.

Why this matters for a CMS

  • The boring parts disappear. Scaffolding document types and seeding realistic content takes minutes.
  • It is real content. Nothing here is a mock-up. Editors can open any page in the backoffice and keep working on it, block by block.
  • The rules still apply. The agent works through the same API, permissions and validation as everyone else, and the project conventions are written down where it can read them.
  • It is verifiable. Every write can be read back. When a payload is wrong, the agent sees that and corrects it.

The takeaway

MCP does not replace the editor or the developer. It removes the distance between deciding what should exist and having it exist. That is why it is awesome.

  • It is real content. Nothing here is a mock-up. Editors can open any page in the backoffice and keep working on it, block by block.
  • The rules still apply. The agent works through the same API, permissions and validation as everyone else, and the project conventions are written down where it can read them.
  • It is verifiable. Every write can be read back. When a payload is wrong, the agent sees that and corrects it.

The takeaway

MCP does not replace the editor or the developer. It removes the distance between deciding what should exist and having it exist. That is why it is awesome.

content.text:
The blog is built and working: all three pages return 200, every block renders through its ViewComponent, and all images load.

## What I built

**Content model (over MCP)**
- **Blocks:** `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock` and `blogPostListBlock`, all filed in the Blocks folder.
- **Data type:** `Blog Block Grid`, a 12-column grid allowing those five blocks.
- **Pages:** `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost`, in the Pages folder, each with a `blocks` grid and its own template.
- **Site root:** `siteRoot` now allows `blogFrontPage` as a child.

**Content (over MCP)**
- **Front page:** "MCP Notes" under WWW with domain `/`, made of a hero, an intro text and the post list.
- **Post 1:** "MCP Is the USB-C Port for AI" (22 September 2026).
- **Post 2:** "This Blog Was Built Without Opening the Backoffice" (29 September 2026).
- **Media:** five Unsplash images in a `Blog` media folder.

**Code (after the restart)**
- Plain view models in [Models/Blocks/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Models/Blocks/)
- One ViewComponent per block in [ViewComponents/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/ViewComponents/), with views in [Views/Shared/Components/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Shared/Components/)
- Adapter partials named by element alias in [Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/)
- [_Layout.cshtml](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml), [blogFrontPage.cshtml](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml) and [blogPost.cshtml](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/blogPost.cshtml), which render blocks with `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`
- Block grid layout and rich text styles in [site.css](Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css)

## How to view it

Umbraco is running now, started from this session.

| Page | URL |
|---|---|
| Front page | https://localhost:44317/ |
| Post 1 | https://localhost:44317/mcp-is-the-usb-c-port-for-ai/ |
| Post 2 | https://localhost:44317/this-blog-was-built-without-opening-the-backoffice/ |
| Backoffice | https://localhost:44317/umbraco (admin@example.com / 1234567890) |

If the site has stopped, run `dotnet run` in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco`.

## Things to know

- **Not everything is a block.** The post's excerpt, list image, publish date and author are page properties, because the post list needs them. The post template also renders the date, author and "All posts" link outside the grid.
- **The CSS bundle is a one-off build.** I ran `npm install` and `npm run build` in `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend`. If you change Tailwind classes in a view, rebuild or run `npm run watch`.
- **`ViewComponents/` is a new folder.** AGENTS.md doesn't say where ViewComponent classes live, so I put them at the project root.
- **Images uploaded by URL get a left-edge focal point.** `create-media` set the focal point to `left: 0`, which crops off-centre. I reset all five to centre and removed `.jpg` from their names with `update-media`.
- **The post list block is allowed on posts too.** There is one grid data type for both page types, so an editor could add the list to a post.

Nothing is broken that I know of; the log shows no errors or warnings beyond the standard application URL notice.
